Environment check performed before this question was written (`podman info`, no database
started): the guest reports **8 CPUs** and **16,496,418,816 B** of memory, which matches
`docs/environments/host-zenbook-ux5406sa.md` and the 2026-09-13 recheck exactly. The
`podman machine list` line showing `4` CPUs and `2GiB` is the machine *definition*, not the
live guest, and it does not indicate an environment mismatch. Client 5.8.1, server 5.8.5.

v1 of the book must be assembled from the five studies already in this repository: no new
study, no new design implementation, no new measurement, and no re-running of anything.

Decide the highest-value set of (a) evidence corrections and (b) model additions that the
already-committed corpus can support, and say what each one changes for a reader.

**(a) Evidence defects.** Name every defect that would mislead a reader if it were
published as-is: claim validity and strength labelling (a claim stronger or weaker than its
trials, controls and environment support); comparability (ratios read across runs, digests,
workloads or environments that are not comparable, and controlled pairs that are missing,
confounded, or that change more than one decision); provenance and reproducibility (missing
run tags, null `repo_commit`, digest or environment mismatches, dirty-tree or unattributed
runs, cells called valid whose gate was weakened); and compliance with the current
methodology minimums (cluster and client sizing, rollup/rolldown/embedding coverage,
colocated versus non-colocated placement, optimistic versus pessimistic concurrency,
negative controls).

**(b) Model additions.** Name the design models the corpus can already support but the book
does not yet present: design families and controlled variants already instantiated by
existing designs but unnamed, ungrouped or mis-grouped in the book taxonomy; and analytic or
decision models the existing evidence can back — cost models, when-to rules, decision trees,
trade-off frameworks, failure-mode catalogues, and rules for reading a benchmark honestly.

For every item state the exact evidence that supports it (run id, report, analysis, digest,
tag or file), whether it can be done from artefacts already committed, what it costs, and
what it must not require. Name the strongest item first: the synthesis must be able to take
the top of each list and act on it without further triage.

## Boundaries

- This brainstorm decides what to correct and add to the book. It authorizes no measurement,
  no new study, no new design implementation and no database start.
- It may not propose editing, relabelling or superseding any existing report, analysis,
  discussion, run, manifest or tag. A correction is a new, attributed artefact that cites the
  old one.
- It must not re-plan work already queued: the evidence registry, the three HIGH reviews,
  the Typst toolchain, book synthesis, the release review, and the six scientific protocol
  tasks listed in the book goal's `BACKLOG.md`.
- This brainstorm creates no tasks. Only the owner's separate
  `CREATE TASKS FROM BRAINSTORM <id>` can publish them.
- Nothing may be upgraded in strength. A single-run directional result stays single-run
  directional; a claim with no repeat stays labelled as it is.
- Outside material may inform a mechanism argument only when explicitly labelled as outside
  material; it can never be the basis of a book claim.
- Items that would need a new run, a new design or a database start are recorded only as
  named gaps, never as recommendations for v1.
